scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Performed by 13 or 17 young boys carrying massive drums, the Gendang Beleq is a sacred marching orchestra of the Sasak people.
on_screen: Title card: Gendang Beleq · Indonesia · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Gendang Beleq dance originates from the Sasak people of Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, with a name derived from a Sasak language term meaning big drum.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Gendang Beleq is performed during life-cycle ceremonies such as births, circumcisions, weddings, and funerals.
It is also performed during rain-invoking ceremonies and national holiday celebrations.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance is executed by a group form of orchestra where musicians simultaneously play, dance, and march.
The ensemble is composed exclusively of males, typically young boys, numbering 13 or 17 participants, centered on two big kendang drum players.
on_screen: Formation: performed in a group form of orchestra
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The orchestra features two main gendang beleqs—the male gendang mama and female gendang nina—which carry the dynamics.
Additional instruments include a Kodeq drum, a sniper rifle, and a code shooter as rhythmic tools, alongside a gong and two reogs (reog nina and reog mama) that carry the melody.
Listen for the gendang beleq, gendang mama, gendang nina, kendang.
